imp_lede.message: Export your passwords from the other app or browser, add the file here and check what changes before anything is imported.

imp_rule.message: Logins for the same site and user become one item. When their passwords differ, the newer one stays and the other goes to the item’s password history: no password is lost.

imp_sub_google.message: The QR codes of Transfer accounts

imp_sub_authy.message: No export: move each code by hand

imp_steps_bitwarden_1.message: In the Bitwarden web vault, open Tools → Export vault. In the apps it’s File → Export vault, or Settings → Export vault.

imp_steps_bitwarden_2.message: Choose the file format .json. Not “.json (Encrypted)”: Klav can’t read that one.

imp_steps_bitwarden_3.message: Confirm with your master password. Bitwarden saves bitwarden_export_….json.

imp_steps_1password_1.message: Open 1Password on your computer and choose File → Export, then the account.

imp_steps_1password_2.message: Pick the 1PUX format and enter your password.

imp_steps_google_1.message: On your phone, open Google Authenticator, open its menu and choose Transfer accounts → Export accounts.

imp_steps_google_2.message: Select the accounts. With many, the app shows several QR codes, one after another: you need all of them.

imp_steps_google_3.message: Take a photo of each QR code with another device and add the pictures here. Or paste the otpauth-migration:// links a QR reader shows. On iPhone, Klav scans them with the camera.

imp_steps_chrome_1.message: Chrome: open chrome://password-manager/settings. Edge: edge://settings/passwords. Brave: brave://password-manager/settings.

imp_steps_chrome_2.message: Choose Export passwords (in Edge it’s under ⋯) and confirm with your computer’s password.

imp_steps_safari_1.message: On macOS 15 or later, open the Passwords app and choose File → Export All Passwords to File.

imp_steps_safari_2.message: On earlier versions, in Safari choose File → Export → Passwords.

imp_steps_safari_3.message: Confirm with Touch ID or your password. It saves Passwords.csv.

imp_steps_csv_1.message: Export a CSV file from the other app.

imp_steps_csv_2.message: Klav reads the columns title (or name), url, username, password, notes, totp and tags.

imp_paste_label.message: Or paste the otpauth-migration:// links, one per line

imp_pasted.description: The name of pasted links in the list of files.

imp_delete_text.message: It holds your passwords in plain text. Delete it and empty the trash:

imp_delete_google.message: The QR codes hold your one-time code secrets: delete their photos too, and the recently deleted ones.

imp_authy_text.message: Authy never offered a way to take your codes out, and its desktop apps closed in 2024. Move each code by making Klav the site’s authenticator, one site at a time:

imp_authy_1.message: Sign in to the site and open its two-factor settings.

imp_authy_2.message: Choose to change the authenticator app, or turn two-factor off and on again. The site shows a new QR code and its setup key.

imp_authy_3.message: Add that setup key to the site’s login in Klav as its one-time code, and type the code Klav shows to confirm.

imp_authy_4.message: Only then remove the site from Authy.

imp_authy_note.message: Klav doesn’t read the file Twilio sends on a data request: its codes are encrypted with a scheme Twilio doesn’t document.

health_breach_notice.message: Klav asks Have I Been Pwned (api.pwnedpasswords.com) about each password. It sends only the first 5 characters of the password's SHA-1 hash, never the password or the whole hash, and the answer is padded so its size gives nothing away. Have I Been Pwned sees your IP address and the time. This device only.
